other: {"answer":"Errors propagate through two layers: inside `compose()` (src/compose.ts) and around it in `Hono#dispatch` (src/hono-base.ts).

1. Inside compose's `dispatch(i)`: each middleware/handler call is wrapped in `try { res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1)) } catch (err) {...}`. If `err instanceof Error` AND an `onError` handler was passed to `compose(...)`, it sets `context.error = err`, calls `res = await onError(err, context)`, and marks `isError = true` — this lets error-handling middleware produce a Response that gets assigned to `context.res` (since the `res && (context.finalized === false || isError)` check allows overwriting even an already-finalized context when `isError` is true). If no onError is configured, or the thrown value isn't an Error, it's rethrown up the promise chain to whichever `dispatch()` call awaited it — i.e., it propagates up through nested middleware layers (each middleware's own `await next()` call site) until caught somewhere, or escapes `compose()` entirely.

2. Hono's `#dispatch` builds the composed chain via `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` (hono-base.ts:451), so `this.errorHandler` (default defined at hono-base.ts:36, or overridden via `app.onError()` at line 272-273) is the `onError` compose receives. The default handler special-cases HTTPException-like errors (`'getResponse' in err`) to reuse their Response, otherwise logs and returns a generic 500.

3. If an error escapes `compose()` entirely (rethrown because no onError, or a non-Error throw), `#dispatch`'s outer `try { const context = await composed(c) } catch (err) { return this.#handleError(err, c) }` (hono-base.ts:455-464) catches it as a final backstop, calling `this.errorHandler` directly via the private `#handleError` method (which rethrows non-Error values rather than handling them — line 400-404).

4. There's also a fast path when a route has exactly one handler (matchResult[0].length === 1, hono-base.ts:430-448) that bypasses `compose()` altogether: it wraps the single handler call in its own try/catch (or `.catch()` for promises) and routes any error straight to `#handleError`, skipping the compose-level onError entirely.

5. A separate compose call also appears at hono-base.ts:226 (`compose([], app.errorHandler)(c, () => r.handler(c, next))`) used for the `.route()`/mounting path — same onError propagation mechanism, scoped per sub-app's errorHandler.

So the propagation path is: inner middleware throw → caught by the nearest enclosing `dispatch()` frame in compose → handled by the configured `onError`/`errorHandler` if present (turning it into a Response) → otherwise rethrown up through each nested `next()` await → escapes `composed(c)` → caught by `#dispatch`'s outer try/catch → `#handleError` → `this.errorHandler` as last resort.</answer>

report.answer: Errors propagate in two layers: inside compose()'s dispatch(i) (src/compose.ts), each handler call is try/caught, and if onError was passed in, it converts the Error into a Response (context.res) via onError(err, context); otherwise it rethrows up through nested next() awaits. Hono#dispatch (src/hono-base.ts) calls compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler), so this.errorHandler (default at hono-base.ts:36, overridable via app.onError()) is the onError compose uses, and any error that still escapes composed(c) is caught by dispatch's outer try/catch and passed to #handleError, which rethrows non-Error values. A separate single-handler fast path (when a route has only one handler) bypasses compose() entirely and routes errors straight to #handleError via its own try/catch/.catch().
